| Clause ② | **not triggered.** ⭐ And note the direction: **lowering** a ratchet ceiling to the measured value is the shrink-only direction. The maintainer's manual floor covers **raising** a ceiling; this is its opposite and needs no escalation. |

### Triage asked me to check one thing before claiming, and the answer is yes — it is already done

> *"re-measure plugin-auth's −12 at claim, it may already be spoken for by another card — check before touching"*

**It is spoken for, and it has already landed.** Read from `origin/main` = `0e0bf8049`:

| entry | recorded ceiling on `main` | card says | status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` | **348** | 348 | in scope ✅ |
| `@objectstack/runtime` | **227** | 227 | in scope ✅ |
| `@objectstack/plugin-auth` | **97** | "109 recorded" | ⛔ **already lowered** — its note reads *"RE-TALLIED from tsc at the 97 below (#10615)"* |

⇒ The card's whole −12 discussion is **stale**, and its warning that "the number on #10615 should not be read as current" has been overtaken: the ledger now records exactly the measured 97. This does not shrink the work — the card already excluded `plugin-auth` — but ⛔ do not be drawn into re-touching it by the card's prose.

**The advisory-line half is confirmed real.** #6376 is `closed` / `completed` (2026-08-08, by `hotlong`, via PR #6510). So the gate's own advisory currently names a dead card as the class tracker for the surpluses it prints on every run. That is the lane's *"a gate's self-description must be true — a gate with a false reason is worse than no gate"* case, and it is arguably the more valuable half of this card.

**Independent corroboration from today.** The dev on #11525 measured `plugin-approvals` at **347** against the recorded **348** this morning and reported it as an out-of-scope finding — and, notably, concluded it was "already tracked by the issue the gate's own message cites (#6376)". That is precisely the dead-end this card exists to close: a careful dev read the advisory, followed it to a closed card, and filed nothing. ⇒ The −1 surplus is corroborated by a second measurement, and the advisory's harm is now measured rather than predicted.

**Serial constraints.** No hot-file collision; nothing in flight touches `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`. **Fold-or-serial:** nothing to fold.

⚠️ **Cost warning for the dev:** `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` refuses to run on an unbuilt closure (by design — it declines to measure a different world). Budget the workspace build; a dev this morning measured it at 70/70 tasks in ~7m12s.

## ACCEPT (on the work) — PR #12110 · ⛔ landing HELD until CI converges

Reviewer of record: devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` (seat #6023).

⏳ **Not flipping ready yet.** 0 failures, but `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and `Test Core (1/6)` are still `in_progress`. The debt-ledger job is the one that actually re-measures this ledger, so it is precisely the wrong one to assume.

### ⭐⭐ Half this card is premise-false, and the dev said so instead of manufacturing work

The card's title claims **two** untracked surpluses. Measured on `origin/main` = `0e0bf8049` with the closure built (70/70 tasks, ~5m34s):

| entry | recorded | measured | outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` | 348 | **347** | lowered ✅ |
| `@objectstack/runtime` | 227 | **227** | ⛔ **no surplus — row is premise-false, left untouched** |

`runtime` measured exactly its recorded value, both before and after. The dev did not lower it, did not invent a justification for touching it, and reported the row as false. ⭐ That is the behaviour Zone 2 asked for in as many words, and it is the one most likely to be quietly skipped — a dev that "found" a −1 on `runtime` to match the card would have produced a green PR and a ledger entry nobody could reconstruct.

⇒ **The card's title is now half wrong.** Leaving it as filed; it closes via `Fixes` and the record of what was actually true is here.

### The re-tally is attributed, not just renumbered

`--lower` writes the number; it cannot tell you *which* error class retired. The dev reproduced `plugin-approvals`' 347-error run standalone and **diffed by error code** against the recorded 348 composition:

> TS2339 ×296, TS2550 ×20, TS2345 ×16, TS18048 ×10, TS2554 ×2, TS1470 ×1, TS2352 ×1, TS6133 ×1 — all unchanged to the unit; **TS2353 (was ×1) is the sole retirement**.

So the note now describes a composition that is true *and* attributable to one identified class, rather than a number that happens to be smaller. It also correctly declined to write a `compositionAt` field, because this entry's TS-code-style note sits outside the reconciler's tier-phrase grammar by the gate's own design — a distinction it would have been easy to paper over.

**Independent corroboration:** #11525's dev measured `plugin-approvals` at 347 this morning from a completely different task. Two measurements, same number.

### ⭐ The #6376 repoint came back better than triage's suggestion

Triage proposed: *"name this card's successor mechanism, or drop the reference."* The dev read #6376 before repointing and found the premise underneath both options was off — **#6376 was never a standing tracker.** It was the design discussion that *shipped* this very surplus-reporting line and the `--lower` remedy. There is no live successor issue to name because the mechanism itself is the remedy.

So the advisory now points at the mechanism rather than at any issue number, and a second stale design comment was repointed with it. ⇒ A gate whose self-description sends readers to a closed card is exactly the *"a gate's reason must be true"* failure — and the honest repair here was to stop citing an issue at all, not to substitute a fresher one that would rot the same way.

### On the open question — already banked, no action needed

The additive `POST /labels` REST endpoint being unreachable (`"GitHub access is not enabled for this session"`) is a **known session-level fact**, not a new gap: this seat hit the same wall today, it is recorded on the seat post, and it is already filed in the skills lane as #11577 / #11573. The documented fallback (read → union → whole-set write via MCP → **read back**) is the prescribed route and the dev used it correctly, including the read-back. ⛔ No new card.

**Next step:** when all three outstanding jobs report `completed` green, flip ready, arm SQUASH, verify by the queue ref. If any goes red — particularly the debt-ledger job — that is this seat's work, not the dev's.
